$comment: Golden fixture for the orchestration-review contract v1 (issue #5146).
Executed by contracts/orchestration-review/v1/test_review_result_contract.py, which
runs in .github/workflows/orchestration-review-contract-tests.yml. This file and
models.py must agree: change one and the other must follow, or CI fails.
Both sides of the contract read THIS file. The gateway consumer
(modules/gateway/tests/orchestration/test_review_evidence.py) validates the same
accepted documents it would receive over the wire, and the worker producer
(modules/agent-factory/agent-worker-image/tests/test_review_result_writer.py)
asserts that what the real runtime assembles validates against the same models.
That is the #4029 lesson: two suites each asserting their own assumption were both
green while the producer and consumer disagreed about two fields for months.
The rejected_* lists below are the substance. Every one of them is a shape that was
actually observed on #5146 or a rule whose absence would let one of those shapes
through, and each must be REJECTED by the models.
The fully-supported approval: functional stage completed, no open blocker, a
formal verdict recorded against the very commit that was reviewed, and a
reviewer run distinct from the author run. Every one of those is load-bearing —
remove any and 'approve' stops validating.
accepted_result_approve.name: orchestration-review

findings.summary: Generated provenance block orders fields differently from the template; cosmetic only.

evidence_refs.summary: Offline suite plus generator/field/provenance checks at the reviewed head.
Contract the generated fixture was checked against; not tied to a commit.

$comment: The security-only run, expressed HONESTLY. This is the shape the observed runs
should have emitted instead of a clean security report: the functional stage is
present with outcome 'not-run' and a reason, the verdict is 'incomplete', and the
missing formal verdict is reported as 'not-attempted' rather than left absent.
It validates on purpose — the contract's job is to make this state representable
and unmistakably non-approving, not to forbid it. approval_blockers() returns
three reasons for this document.
accepted_result_security_only_incomplete.name: orchestration-review

stages.name: functional
stages.detail: Functional review was not performed; the run produced only a security report.

findings.summary: The destructive-apply gate fails open; filtered below the security reporting threshold but a functional merge blocker.

evidence_refs.summary: Reproduction recorded during the security stage at this head.

publication.detail: The run ended after its security report without attempting a formal verdict.

$comment: Both stages completed, no blocking finding, and the provider REFUSED to record
the verdict because the reviewer shares the author's bot identity — the
shared-identity case tracked under #4660.
Note the verdict is 'request-changes', not 'approve': an unpublished verdict is
an approval blocker, so 'approve' would fail validation here. That is the rule
working as intended — a refused publication cannot be smoothed into an approval.
The refusal detail is reported, which is what the observed runs never did.
accepted_result_publication_refused.name: orchestration-review

findings.summary: Diagnostic data is retained in the emitted payload and must be removed before merge.

evidence_refs.summary: Functional suite executed at the reviewed head.

publication.detail: The provider refused the formal review: the reviewer identity matches the pull-request author identity.

rejected_variants.name: security_only_stage_list
rejected_variants.why: The exact observed defect: a result describing ONLY the security stage. Without the mandatory-functional-stage rule this validates and then reads as 'nothing blocking found'. A security-only run must instead report functional as 'not-run' with a reason.

rejected_variants.name: empty_stage_list
rejected_variants.why: A result that describes no review stage at all is not review evidence.

rejected_variants.name: duplicate_stage_name
rejected_variants.why: Two outcomes for one stage is ambiguous: a consumer cannot tell whether functional review concluded.

rejected_variants.name: unexplained_not_run_stage
rejected_variants.why: A 'not-run' stage with no reason is the silent skip this contract exists to make noisy.

rejected_variants.name: self_review
rejected_variants.why: The reviewer run is the author run. A run cannot review its own output.

rejected_variants.name: approve_with_open_blocking_finding
rejected_variants.why: An 'approve' verdict alongside an open blocking finding. This is the U19 shape: correctness blockers the security stage filtered below threshold must survive into the verdict.

findings.summary: workspace_cluster is unbound on the replacement path.

rejected_variants.name: approve_with_acknowledged_blocker
rejected_variants.why: Acknowledging a blocking finding does not clear it; only 'resolved' with evidence does. Otherwise a reviewer could approve past any blocker by noting it.

findings.summary: workspace_cluster is unbound on the replacement path.

rejected_variants.name: approve_with_unpublished_verdict
rejected_variants.why: The most-repeated observed failure: both stages complete, verdict approve, and no formal verdict recorded anywhere repository rules can read it.

publication.detail: the run ended before publishing a formal verdict

rejected_variants.name: approve_with_functional_stage_not_run
rejected_variants.why: An 'approve' verdict while the functional stage did not run. Present-but-not-run must still block approval, not merely be recorded.

rejected_variants.name: publication_head_differs_from_reviewed_head
rejected_variants.why: The wrong-revision defect: a formal verdict recorded against a commit the reviewer never inspected. Observed when a review analysed 628842d5 and the provider attached the verdict to f0d2eb96.

rejected_variants.name: published_without_head_sha
rejected_variants.why: A 'published' publication that does not name the commit it was recorded against cannot be checked for the wrong-revision defect at all.

rejected_variants.name: resolved_blocking_finding_without_evidence
rejected_variants.why: 'Fixed, trust me'. The observed false-negative claimed all six blockers fixed having re-tested one sub-behaviour; a blocking finding declared resolved must carry the evidence that showed it.

findings.summary: SETTINGS approval was unreachable for an image/network pin change.

rejected_variants.name: duplicate_finding_id
rejected_variants.why: A repeated finding_id makes 'is this blocker resolved?' unanswerable — one entry can say open and the other resolved.

rejected_variants.name: short_reviewed_head_sha
rejected_variants.why: An abbreviated commit id is ambiguous and no provider issues one. Head binding is worthless if the head can be a prefix.

rejected_variants.name: uppercase_reviewed_head_sha
rejected_variants.why: Mixed case would make two spellings of one commit compare unequal, silently producing a false stale-head refusal.

rejected_variants.name: missing_provider_repository_id
rejected_variants.why: Only the mutable display name is supplied. A rename or transfer re-points it, which is how findings land on the wrong repository.

rejected_variants.name: missing_provider_pr_node_id
rejected_variants.why: PR number alone is not immutable identity; the contract refuses to bind on it, mirroring PullRequestIdentity's INCOMPLETE_IDENTITY arm.

rejected_variants.name: naive_observed_at
rejected_variants.why: A timestamp with no zone means 'whatever the writer's clock said', and this artifact is read by a different machine than wrote it.

rejected_variants.name: zero_claim_generation
rejected_variants.why: Generations start at 1. Zero would compare as older than every real generation and could never be recognised as current.

rejected_variants.name: negative_accepted_plan_version
rejected_variants.why: 0 is legal and means 'no accepted plan' (the legacy path). Negative is not a version.

rejected_variants.name: blank_org_id
rejected_variants.why: A blank tenant is not a tenant. Every read and write is scoped to it, so a blank one belongs to everyone and no one.

rejected_variants.name: zero_cycle
rejected_variants.why: Cycles start at 1; cycle 0 cannot be distinguished from 'unset'.

rejected_variants.name: unknown_severity_value
rejected_variants.why: A closed vocabulary: an unrecognised severity must be a validation error, never something that falls through to 'not blocking'.

findings.summary: Severity value is not in the vocabulary.

rejected_variants.name: unknown_disposition_value
rejected_variants.why: Same argument for dispositions: an unknown value must not read as cleared.

findings.summary: Disposition value is not in the vocabulary.

rejected_variants.name: unknown_publication_outcome
rejected_variants.why: An unrecognised publication outcome must not be treated as published.

rejected_variants.name: unknown_verdict_value
rejected_variants.why: The verdict vocabulary is closed so a typo cannot become a permit.

rejected_variants.name: extra_top_level_field
rejected_variants.why: extra='forbid'. An unmodelled field is either a producer bug or a consumer that will ignore something the producer thought was load-bearing.

rejected_variants.name: wrong_contract_name
rejected_variants.why: A document from another contract must not validate as this one.

rejected_variants.name: wrong_contract_version
rejected_variants.why: A different version is a different contract file.

rejected_variants.name: wrong_contract_owner
rejected_variants.why: The owning surface is pinned so a forged envelope cannot claim this contract.

rejected_variants.name: blank_result_id
rejected_variants.why: A result with no identifier cannot be deduplicated or referenced.

rejected_variants.name: missing_publication
rejected_variants.why: Publication is mandatory. Making it optional is exactly how 'the formal verdict never happened' became unrepresentable in the observed runs.

rejected_variants.name: missing_lineage
rejected_variants.why: Without lineage there is no self-review check and no attributable reviewer.

rejected_variants.name: missing_subject
rejected_variants.why: Without a subject there is no reviewed commit, which is the entire point of the contract.

rejected_variants.name: missing_authority
rejected_variants.why: Without accepted plan version and claim generation, nothing fences this result against work someone else now owns.
